{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOV5s7_c8AAAABiVY4Xw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bs-hLzhLso7s", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bs-hL", "number": 7, "title": "Add Famicom Disk System support with automatic media selection and a unified game UI", "body": "## Goal and scope

Add a playable Famicom Disk System (FDS) baseline to the existing NES emulator delivered by #3. Prioritize this work now, before further general NES mapper expansion or hardware-accuracy improvements; only fix shared-core deficiencies that are necessary for the FDS baseline or to prevent regressions. Build on the current `main` and retain the shared Rust core, Wasm adapter, native runner and static frontend.

**One emulator, one game library, one game-opening flow.** The user opens a game, and the emulator automatically selects cartridge NES or FDS hardware based on the validated media format. There must be no manual NES/FDS mode selector, separate FDS page or parallel game library. Preserve the existing snes-rust-derived visual design, controls and interaction flows; show only the additional controls needed by the currently loaded disk game.

### Deliverables

- [ ] Introduce a shared media abstraction and transactional staging/loading path for existing iNES `.nes` cartridges and `.fds` disk images. Recognize and validate both standard headered and headerless FDS images, including single-sided, double-sided and multi-disk images; reject inconsistent sizes, malformed headers and unsupported formats with clear errors. Do not rely solely on filename extensions. Preserve the running game and its recoverable saves when a selection is cancelled or validation/restoration fails.
- [ ] Implement the FDS RAM adapter and hardware in Rust, sharing the existing NTSC CPU/PPU/APU and controller implementation: 32 KiB program RAM, 8 KiB CHR RAM, 8 KiB user-supplied BIOS mapping, nametable mirroring, timer/disk IRQs, drive motor and transfer state, disk read/write registers, insertion/ejection and side changes. Implement disk timing, block/gap/CRC handling and write behavior as required for the tested baseline; document any hardware approximations and unsupported image variants. Execute BIOS/game instructions through the generic emulated CPU, not game-specific boot shortcuts.
- [ ] Implement the FDS expansion audio (wave RAM, frequency, envelope and modulation behavior) and mix it with the NES APU output through the existing native/Wasm audio path. Include deterministic numerical and guest-program regression tests.
- [ ] Extend the existing cartridge picker into a single **Open game** / change-game flow accepting local `.nes` and `.fds` files, with one mixed remembered-game list (e.g. **My games**). Existing stored cartridges and saves must remain usable without reimport or migration-related data loss. Automatically start the appropriate machine after successful loading; selecting a remembered game follows the same path. Keep existing keyboard/gamepad/touch, Play/Pause/Reset, CRT/Pixel, scale, fullscreen, mute/volume and hidden-tab behavior.
- [ ] On the first FDS load, if no valid BIOS is available, prompt for a lawfully obtained local 8 KiB FDS BIOS (e.g. `disksys.rom`) inline in the loading flow, validate size and document the supported BIOS identity/validation policy. Allow cancellation without replacing the previous game. Remember a successfully supplied BIOS locally for subsequent FDS games, and provide a minimal way to replace or forget it within the existing picker/help flow, without a separate settings page. Never bundle, fetch, link to unauthorized downloads of, or upload BIOS bytes. No BIOS is needed for ordinary NES games.
- [ ] After a successful FDS load, start with the first available side inserted. Interpret the sides in image order and expose only actual available sides, e.g. Disk 1 — A, Disk 1 — B, Disk 2 — A, etc. One disk side is physically inserted at a time. Provide a compact side selector and eject/insert operation only while an FDS game is active, including in fullscreen where needed for gameplay. Side changes must emulate ejection/reinsertion and relevant timing/status transitions without resetting the machine, reloading the file or losing progress. Do not add automatic disk swapping in this baseline. Keep the FDS controls available when the drive is empty; hide them when an NES cartridge or no game is active.
- [ ] Keep original disk-image bytes immutable; persist writes for all sides locally using stable identity derived from the original disk content, with a documented policy for headered/headerless equivalents. Preserve progress across disk changes, reset, NES/FDS switching, and browser reload/reopening. Use the existing storage and multi-tab coordination mechanisms or equivalent safeguards. Distinguish disk saves from cartridge battery RAM; removing a library entry must not silently delete its saved progress. Failed reads/restoration or writes must not silently overwrite or lose recoverable data. Never modify the user's original local file.
- [ ] Extend the native runner and Wasm staging/runtime interface for disk media, BIOS, side operations and disk-save data. Add reproducible source-generated diagnostic BIOS/guest fixtures or independently audited legally usable test inputs covering read/write/IRQ/audio and multi-side gameplay. Demonstrate at least one genuinely interactive FDS program/game executing via the shared CPU/PPU/APU/FDS implementation, not just a BIOS screen or simulated UI. The mandatory automated gates must run without a proprietary BIOS or commercial disk image; use a suitable original test BIOS and source-built disk guest, and document exactly what real-BIOS compatibility is and is not verified. Optional manual tests may use a lawfully supplied real BIOS and games, without distributing them.
- [ ] Update README, compatibility information, help and reproducible test commands. Keep all ROM, BIOS and disk binaries out of the tracked tree and production build. Generated or audited fetched test fixtures are test-only and ignored; document their provenance, rights and hashes. No built-in ROMs, disk games or BIOS, automatic media downloads, or network transmission of user media, names or save data.

Scope boundaries: a playable NTSC FDS baseline, not exhaustive disk-drive electrical accuracy, every BIOS variant, every commercial title, alternative disk formats (e.g. QD), automatic side detection/swapping, save states or unrelated NES improvements. Document limitations rather than claiming unverified compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Existing regression gates:** Run the current README test commands from a clean checkout: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `node tests/roms/check.mjs`, `cargo build --locked -p nes-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release`, `npm --prefix web ci`, `npm --prefix web run build`, `npm --prefix web test` (with the documented Chromium installation), `node tests/check-static.mjs` and `git diff --check`. Update fixture/static checks to cover FDS as appropriate. All pass, including existing cartridge replay, mapper, save and browser tests. CI runs the applicable new checks without proprietary assets.
- [ ] **Format and hardware:** Run documented deterministic native tests for headered/headerless parsing, malformed and truncated images, single-side and multi-disk enumeration, BIOS validation/mapping, RAM/CHR/mirroring, timer and disk IRQ acknowledgement, bounded transfer timing, read/write behavior, drive state and side changes. Assert expected bytes, registers, interrupts and state transitions. Test eject/no-media and write-protect behavior where supported; explicitly document unsupported behavior. Run numerical expansion-audio tests for wave output, envelope/modulation and mixing with NES audio. All required vectors pass.
- [ ] **End-to-end FDS execution:** Run a reproducible source-built FDS guest with a legally usable test BIOS through the native runner and actual browser Wasm core. Demonstrate boot, disk reads, controller-driven state/video changes, non-silent FDS-generated audio, a required side change without resetting the machine, and disk writes that are subsequently read back. Include a multi-disk fixture with at least three sides and a single-side fixture. Record hashes, bounded execution/replay commands, expected checkpoints and results; distinguish test-BIOS evidence from actual Nintendo BIOS/game compatibility.
- [ ] **Unified UX:** Use real-browser automation to open local NES and FDS files from the same picker, select both from one remembered-game list, switch NES -> FDS -> NES and back, and verify automatic hardware selection without a mode toggle. Test missing/invalid BIOS, cancellation, successful registration, reuse, replacement/removal and invalid media while a game is running. Expected: successful loads start the selected game, failed/cancelled loads preserve the previous machine and play/pause state, NES never requires a BIOS, and only FDS exposes disk controls. Test all enumerated sides, eject/reinsert and side switching while running, including one-sided media without phantom sides. Record desktop and mobile portrait/landscape/fullscreen screenshots against the existing frontend. Existing layout, controls, styling and defaults remain recognizably unchanged except necessary media labels and FDS controls.
- [ ] **Persistence and safety:** In isolated browser profiles, write distinct known bytes to multiple FDS sides, change sides, reset, switch to NES, reopen/reload and assert exact restored disk content. Verify different games do not share saves, original local inputs remain unchanged, previous NES cartridge library/saves survive upgrade, and BIOS stays local. Exercise storage read/write errors, concurrent tabs, removal/reimport and retry; expected: no silent loss or stale overwrite of recoverable saves and useful recovery messages. Use request tracing to verify no BIOS, ROM, disk, filenames or save data are sent over the network.
- [ ] **No bundled media and documentation:** Inspect `git ls-files`, generated artifacts in `web/dist`, embedded resources, fixture provenance and startup requests. Expected: no distributed ROM/BIOS/FDS binaries or embedded demo payloads, no automatic media fetches, startup remains empty, and only local user-supplied media is opened. Verify the documented build/test commands, supported formats, BIOS requirements, disk controls, persistence and limitations. Record all mandatory checks and expected/actual results in the PR or linked validation document. No mandatory human confirmation is required.

## Post-merge verification

- After the complete PR merges to `main` and this Issue closes, verify the GitHub Pages workflow succeeds. Record the deployment run and actual site URL (expected https://takahirox.github.io/nes-rust-neo/).
- Open the live site in a browser with locally generated/audited test media. Verify the shared picker, NES -> FDS -> NES automatic selection, missing-BIOS prompt, local BIOS reuse, disk-side controls and persistence after reload, and actual FDS video/audio. Confirm the published build includes no bundled media and does not upload user media or saves.
- Record results in the merged PR or closed Issue; open a linked follow-up Issue if publication exposes a defect.
